text: The vectors are integer 24-tuples whose residues modulo two belong to the fixed Golay code. Their pairing is half the dot product, giving the usual real Construction A lattice after dividing coordinates by √2 ([Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)). Division occurs in ℚ, with no integer rounding. The supplied code property ensures all pairings are integers. Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass. Additional [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L44) passes, [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L51) passes.

The two names denote the same vectors and pairing: integer lifts of the fixed Golay code, paired by half their dot product ([Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)). This is equality of the actual constructions. The extra Lean argument certifies integer-valued pairings; it neither selects different vectors nor changes the form. Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass. “Doubly even” means each codeword has a number of nonzero coordinates divisible by four. For any integer lift z, Σzᵢ² is congruent to that number modulo four. Therefore its squared length Σzᵢ²/2 is an even integer, as in [Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4). Lean divides in ℚ here, so no rounding occurs. Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass.

The hypothesis says codewords pair to zero modulo two, making the lattice integral. Its squared lengths are Σzᵢ²/2 in ℚ, without rounding. Since integer squares reduce to their binary residues modulo four, all these lengths are even exactly when every codeword weight is divisible by four: Lean’s “doubly even” condition ([Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4)). Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass.
Golay positive definiteness
Golay evenness
Golay unimodularity

Lean’s hammingNorm counts nonzero coordinates, and “4 ∣ hammingNorm x” says that count is a multiple of four. Integer lifts have squared length Σzᵢ²/2, which is even precisely under that condition ([Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4)). The division is rational, without rounding; the supplied hypothesis ensures integer-valued pairings. Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass. Additional [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Even.lean#L159) passes.

“IsIsotropic C” means every codeword has quadratic value zero in ℚ/ℤ. Here that value is Σzᵢ²/(2m), using rational division and identifying numbers differing by an integer. Its vanishing says the squared length Σzᵢ²/m is even ([Munemasa–Tamura §4](https://arxiv.org/html/1006.2414v3#S4)). The hypotheses require nonzero even m, ensuring independence of the chosen integer lifts. Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass. Additional [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Even.lean#L59) passes.
Exact integer-lift divisibility

Every lattice vector comes from an integer lift z of a codeword and has squared length Σzᵢ²/m ([Harada–Munemasa–Venkov §2](https://www.math.is.tohoku.ac.jp/~munemasa/documents/F3-28.pdf#page=2)). Division is in ℚ, without rounding; this length is an even integer exactly when 2m divides Σzᵢ² in ℤ. Lean’s bracketed NeZero m assumption excludes m=0. The statement quantifies over every lift. Golay checks: [positive definite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L68), [even](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L73), [unimodular](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Golay/Basic.lean#L78) pass. Additional [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/ConstructionA/Even.lean#L113) passes.

Points valued in an algebra B are coordinate-algebra maps to B; the inclusion’s image consists exactly of maps killing I. Normality therefore agrees on every value algebra, exactly as in [Milne, Definition 1.51](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=32). [The coordinate criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Basic.lean#L252) checks the bridge. Arbitrary commutative base rings are allowed; testing only rational points would not establish this statement.
Coordinate normality is equivalent to normality of all value-algebra point subgroups.

The ideal ker f defines the image subgroup. Conjugation equivariance sends ker f into ker(id⊗f); flatness identifies this with the ideal generated by H⊗ker f, giving [Milne, Definition 1.51](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=32). [Normality of a product image](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L221) checks the application. Flatness of H, K and H/ker f is explicit; the lift needs no action laws.
Simultaneous conjugation makes the image of a product of two normal subgroups normal.

Conjugation stability at rational points makes the defining equations vanish in H⊗(H/I); reduced finite-type point separation then proves scheme normality, using [Stacks, Tag 00FV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00FV). [Normality of a subgroup’s identity component](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L126) checks the application. The algebraically closed base, reduced ambient algebra and reduced quotient are all explicit and cannot be replaced by unrestricted rational-point reasoning.
The reduced characteristic identity component of a normal subgroup is normal.

A function in I vanishes on every algebraically closed point of H/J, so its quotient class is zero by [Stacks, Tag 00FV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00FV). Larger defining ideals mean smaller subgroups, so reverse point-subgroup inclusion gives I≤J. [The equality criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Separation.lean#L81) checks orientation. Only H/J must be reduced and finite type; no such assumption on H/I is needed.
Applying point separation twice recovers equality of reduced finite-type subgroup ideals.

Here the bottom point subgroup means the identity alone. Its vanishing functions form the augmentation ideal, so its closure again has only the identity point, matching [Milne, 1.45–1.48](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=30). [The actual equality with augmentation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Vanishing.lean#L243) checks the stronger scheme-level identification. No algebraic closedness, finite type or reducedness of H is assumed; the conclusion here is equality of rational-point subgroups.
The vanishing ideal of the trivial point subgroup equals augmentation scheme-theoretically.

Fixing either argument makes commutator evaluation a regular function; extending its vanishing first across T and then across S proves the displayed rational-point containment. This matches [Milne, §6.d](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=142). [The derived-length application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Derived/PointClosure.lean#L146) checks its use. Closures mean vanishing-ideal closures over any field, without finite-type or algebraic-closedness assumptions.
Commutator closure containment and its trivial endpoint lower the derived-length bound for the actual derived subgroup.

Idempotence puts f(x)−x in ker f, so annihilating that kernel is equivalent to g∘f=g. Here mapDomain is precomposition, so this identifies the coordinate image of [Milne, 3.13–3.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79) with fixed points. [The splitting identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Idempotent.lean#L34) checks scheme-level compatibility. Every commutative value algebra is allowed, including nonreduced ones; rational-point equality alone would be weaker.
The idempotent image factorization is a split retraction.

The coordinate map f:H→K represents a group map in the reverse direction; its image has coordinates H/ker f, which embed into K after every field extension. Idempotents therefore remain trivial when Spec K is geometrically connected, matching the image convention of [Milne, 3.13–3.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). [The actual multiplication-image application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Radical/Product.lean#L64) checks contravariance. No finite-type hypothesis is required, and geometric connectedness is stronger than connectedness over the base alone.
Actual normal-product image of radical candidates is geometrically connected.

The image of the group map Spec K→Spec H has coordinates H/ker f. After each field extension this algebra still injects into K; a nilpotent must therefore vanish when K is geometrically reduced. This uses the coordinate-image convention of [Milne, 3.13–3.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). [The smooth-image consequence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Image/Smooth.lean#L61) checks the geometric hypothesis. No finite type or perfectness of the ground field is assumed here.
Geometric reducedness of the image gives smoothness when the ambient coordinates are finite type.

For the group map Spec K→Spec H, smoothness of the source makes K geometrically reduced; this descends to H/ker f, whose finite type follows from H. The group-specific criterion [Milne, Proposition 1.26](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=24) then gives smoothness. [The normal-product application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Unipotent/Radical/Product.lean#L78) checks the hypotheses. Finite type is imposed on the ambient group’s coordinates H, and no claim about arbitrary images of smooth schemes is made.
Actual normal-product image of radical candidates is smooth.

Coinvariants are functions fixed by translation by kernel points. This invariance equalizes the two maps K→K⊗[H]K; [Mathlib’s effective equalizer criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/IncludeLeftSubRight.lean#L84) identifies their equalizer with the coordinate map’s range. [The faithfully flat specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Coinvariants.lean#L121) checks the resulting equality of subalgebras. Effectiveness is explicitly relative to f’s algebra structure; it need not make f injective or identify that range abstractly with H.
Faithful flatness specializes effective kernel-invariant descent.

Here ofConv evaluates a coordinate function at an algebra-valued group point. If g and g′ have the same image, g⁻¹g′ belongs to the scheme kernel; right invariance makes x take the same value on both points. This is the fiber interpretation behind [Milne, Theorem 5.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=112). [The converse criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Coinvariants.lean#L61) checks the statement. It needs neither flatness nor surjectivity and allows any universe of value algebras.
Constancy on all value-algebra fibers is equivalent to kernel coinvariance.

Coinvariants mean coordinate functions fixed by right translation by the kernel. These translates lie in the same fiber, while any two points in one fiber differ by such a translate. This yields the invariant-function criterion underlying [Milne, Theorem 5.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=112). [The effective descent theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Coinvariants.lean#L81) checks its substantive use. Testing all value algebras in the coordinate universe retains infinitesimal information.
The tensor self-product applies the fiber criterion to recover the coordinate range.

Faithful flatness supplies the effective equalizer property, so functions invariant under the scheme kernel are exactly coordinate pullbacks, as in [Milne, Theorem 5.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=112). [Descent of invariant idempotents](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Coinvariants.lean#L163) checks the result. The theorem works over arbitrary commutative base rings without finite presentation, smoothness or finite type; faithful flatness concerns f itself.
An invariant idempotent descends to an actual idempotent under faithful flatness.
The actual normal-coinvariant factor of a faithfully flat map with the prescribed kernel is bijective.

The counit ε evaluates functions at the identity; augmentation consists of functions vanishing there. Zero precomposition kills their images and the generated kernel ideal by Leibniz. Conversely, subtracting ε(x) reduces every x to augmentation. This is [Milne, 10.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=201). [The zero-composite identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Tangent.lean#L203) checks the differential convention. Arbitrary commutative base and coefficient algebras are allowed, without flatness or smoothness.
The differential vanishes after inclusion of its scheme kernel.

Lie vectors are derivations at the identity. Those annihilating the subgroup’s defining ideal form its Lie algebra; the preceding criterion identifies those exactly with the differential kernel, as in [Milne, 10.14](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=201). [The canonical-equivalence value formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Kernel/Tangent.lean#L188) checks the actual inclusion. The equality is of Lie subalgebras over B, with no field, finite-dimensionality or smoothness hypothesis.
The kernel Lie equivalence is the actual quotient-induced inclusion on ambient values.

The bottom defining ideal is zero, hence represents the entire ambient group. A smooth subgroup with the full Lie algebra fills a connected ambient group, exactly the conclusion of [Milne, Proposition 10.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=202). [The characteristic-zero rigidity application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Tangent/Rigidity.lean#L58) checks the use. Lean explicitly assumes ambient smoothness and an algebraically closed field; subgroup connectedness is unnecessary, but removing its smoothness would admit the αₚ⊂Ga counterexample.
In characteristic zero, the smooth equalizer with full Lie algebra proves equality of homomorphisms from a connected finite-type group.

The identity component is cut out by 1−e for its component idempotent, and every derivation kills idempotents. Thus it has the entire tangent Lie algebra, as noted after [Milne, Proposition 10.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=202). [The idempotent-derivative identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/RingTheory/Derivation/Idempotent.lean#L29) checks the mechanism. Finite type and algebraic closedness are present; smoothness and reducedness are not required.
A derivation kills an idempotent in arbitrary characteristic, without dividing by 2.

Here H/I is the subgroup’s coordinate algebra. Taking its identity component preserves the tangent space; pulling back along the quotient identifies the same subalgebra of the ambient Lie algebra. This matches [Milne, 2.37 and 10.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=202). [The actual quotient comparison square](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/IdentityComponent.lean#L97) checks the embedding. Neither the subgroup nor the ambient group is assumed smooth or reduced.
The two presentations of a subgroup identity component commute with ambient coordinate restriction.
The identity component has all tangent vectors before pulling back into an ambient group.

The identity component is preserved by every automorphism of the subgroup, so ambient conjugations preserve it; reduced rational-point separation upgrades this to scheme normality. This agrees with [Milne, Proposition 1.52](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=32). [The characteristic-ideal identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Connected/Characteristic.lean#L35) checks the premise. Lean retains reducedness of both ambient and subgroup coordinates over an algebraically closed field; ambient connectedness is unnecessary.
Every actual Hopf automorphism preserves the component defining ideal.

A space with arbitrarily small compact neighborhoods has a compact neighborhood at each point. The source applies the stronger local-compactness property to the universal neighborhood. This is exactly the implication from Wendl’s Definition7.19 to condition(i) of Theorem7.20, with no Hausdorff hypothesis needed in this direction. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L143).

An open subspace of a locally compact space is locally compact with the inherited topology. A neighborhood in that subspace contains an ambient neighborhood of its point lying inside the open subset; an ambient compact neighborhood can then be chosen there. The declaration correctly needs no Hausdorff assumption. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L225).

Every compact space is weakly locally compact because the entire space is a compact neighborhood of each point. The source uses exactly that witness. Its conclusion is the one-compact-neighborhood condition, so no Hausdorff assumption or compact neighborhood refinement property is being silently inferred from compactness. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L37).

The product of two locally compact spaces is locally compact. A neighborhood rectangle can be refined in each coordinate to compact neighborhoods, whose product is compact and remains a neighborhood inside the original set. This uses the binary product topology and compact-product theorem without separation assumptions. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L88).

A closed subspace of a locally compact space is locally compact. Intersecting a sufficiently small ambient compact neighborhood with the closed subset gives a compact subspace neighborhood inside the prescribed subspace neighborhood. Closed subsets of compact sets remain compact without Hausdorffness, matching the declaration’s unrestricted ambient topology. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L221).

In a locally compact space, a compact set K inside an open set U has a compact neighborhood L contained in U. The inclusion K⊆interior(L) means that L contains a neighborhood of every point of K. This matches Wendl Exercise7.6; neither Hausdorffness nor closedness of L is assumed. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L173).

If X is locally compact, every continuous map f:X→Y has the following property: any neighborhood of f(x) contains the image of some compact neighborhood of x. Its inverse image is a neighborhood of x, which can be compactly refined. This explains the locally compact pair condition for any topological target Y. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L139).

Given x in open U, local compactness produces compact K⊆U with x in its interior. Interior membership says precisely that K is a neighborhood of x, so this is the open-neighborhood form of Wendl’s Definition7.19. The chosen compact subset is not required to be closed. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L149).

A binary product of weakly locally compact spaces is weakly locally compact. At a given pair, choose one compact neighborhood in each coordinate; their product is compact and is a neighborhood of the pair. The conclusion preserves this weaker condition without requiring arbitrary compact neighborhood refinements. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L23).

An open embedding identifies its domain homeomorphically with an open subset of the target. If the target is locally compact, that open subset has arbitrarily small compact neighborhoods, which transfer back to the domain. This proves local compactness of the domain without requiring either space to be Hausdorff. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L213).

A product of finitely many spaces, each having a compact neighborhood at every point, has the same property. Choose compact neighborhoods of the coordinates; their product is compact. Finitely many coordinate restrictions define a neighborhood in the product topology. The factors may differ, and no Hausdorff assumption is required. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L30).

For a compact and locally compact space Y, the power Y^ι is locally compact in the product topology for any index set ι. A basic neighborhood restricts finitely many coordinates; refine those compactly and leave all others unrestricted. Compactness of Y and Tychonoff make the resulting neighborhood compact. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L133).

Every neighborhood U of a point x in a locally compact space contains a compact neighborhood K of x. Here a neighborhood need not be open: it must contain an open set around x. This is exactly the compact-neighborhood refinement definition of local compactness used by Wendl; no Hausdorff assumption is needed. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L77).

A finite power Y^ι of a locally compact space is locally compact in the product topology. Each coordinate neighborhood can be compactly refined, and finitely many such refinements form a compact neighborhood of the tuple. Thus the index set must be finite, but Y itself need not be compact. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/LocallyCompact.lean#L129).

Two preconnected subsets sharing the specified point x have preconnected union. The common point prevents an open separation from placing the two subsets on different sides, exactly the union argument in Wendl’s proof of Proposition7.5. Membership of x in both sets supplies the required overlap explicitly. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L120).

A continuous image of a space admitting no separation into two nonempty open parts also admits no such separation. This is the meaning of preconnectedness here, which permits the empty space. A separation of the range would pull back to one of the domain, proving the stated continuous-image result. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L722).

The range of a continuous map from a nonempty connected space is nonempty and connected. A point of the domain supplies a point of the range, while any separation of the range would pull back to a separation of the domain. Nonemptiness is included in the declaration’s connected-space hypothesis. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L726).

Every subset containing x and admitting no separation lies in the connected component of x. That component is the union of all such subsets, so this is its maximality property. Although preconnectedness alone permits an empty set, the membership assumption x∈s ensures nonemptiness here, matching the usual connected-subset formulation. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L552).

If y belongs to the connected component of x, the components of x and y are equal. Each component is connected and contains its defining point, so maximality gives the two containments. This is the pointed form of Wendl’s result that connected components are identical or disjoint. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L576).

The connected component of x is connected and nonempty. It is the union of all subsets containing x that admit no separation; their common point prevents their union from separating. The singleton {x} ensures that x belongs to the union. This verifies both connectedness and nonemptiness in the stated conclusion. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Basic.lean#L544).

A subset is compact in its ambient space exactly when it is compact as a space in its own right, with the inherited subspace topology. These are the same finite-open-cover condition: open sets in the subspace are intersections with ambient open sets. This matches Wendl’s observation following Definition5.2. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1051).

Every indexed family of open sets covering a compact subset contains a finite subfamily that still covers it. The conclusion selects a finite set of indices from the original family; the index set itself may be arbitrary. This is exactly Wendl’s open-cover definition, derived from the equivalent filter formulation. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L208).

A function continuous on a compact subset has compact image. Continuity is required only for its restriction to that subset with the inherited topology, so behavior elsewhere is irrelevant. Wendl’s continuous-image theorem therefore applies to exactly the stated domain. The source carries a cluster point forward to establish compactness. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L110).

A closed subset t of a compact set s is compact. The source identifies t with the intersection s∩t and invokes compactness of an intersection with a closed set. This matches Wendl’s Proposition5.8, with ambient closedness of t stated explicitly and no separation assumption. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L105).

A compact space with the discrete topology has a finite underlying set. Every singleton is open, so the family of all singleton sets is an open cover. Compactness selects finitely many of them covering the whole space, which consequently has finitely many points, as in Wendl’s Example5.3. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L909).

The Cartesian product of two compact subsets is compact in the product topology. The proof projects an ultrafilter to each factor, obtains limits inside the two subsets, and combines coordinate convergence. This realizes the binary case of Tychonoff’s theorem with no Hausdorff or nonempty-factor assumptions. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1071).

The union of two compact subsets is compact. Any open cover restricts to a cover of each subset, and the union of the two finite subcovers covers their union. The source specializes its finite-union theorem to two sets, exactly matching Wendl’s Example5.7 without requiring either subset closed. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L520).

Every finite subset of a topological space is compact. The source expresses it as the finite union of its singleton subsets, each compact, matching the finite selection argument in Wendl’s Example5.4. No separation or discreteness assumption is needed, and the empty finite subset is included. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L504).

The domain of a closed embedding into a compact space is compact. Its image is a closed subset of the compact codomain, hence compact; the embedding identifies the domain with that image topologically. The source follows these two steps, with closedness supplied by the embedding hypothesis. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1066).

Suppose the domain topology is pulled back along f: every domain open set is an inverse image of a target open set. This is the inducing-map hypothesis; f need not be injective. A compact K contained in its range has compact inverse image, because open covers transfer across f. [Clark](https://plclark.github.io/PeteLClark/Expositions/pointset.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1011).

An open set containing the product of compact subsets s and t contains a rectangle u×v with u and v open and containing s and t respectively. This is Clark’s generalized tube lemma, using his quasi-compact convention. The source obtains the rectangle from the equality of compact-set neighborhood filters. [Clark](https://plclark.github.io/PeteLClark/Expositions/pointset.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L746).

If a family of closed sets has intersection disjoint from compact s, some finite subfamily already has intersection disjoint from s. Taking complements turns this into the finite-subcover property. It is the relative contrapositive of the finite-intersection characterization of compactness, with ambient closedness stated explicitly. [Khatchatourian](https://www.math.toronto.edu/ivan/mat327/docs/notes/17-tychonoff.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L284).

A neighborhood U(x) assigned to every point of compact s admits a finite subcover with centers chosen in s. Neighborhoods need not themselves be open: their interiors cover s, and compactness selects finitely many centers. The source implements that reduction and explicitly retains membership of each selected center in s. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L236).

A nonempty family of nonempty compact closed sets, directed toward smaller sets, has nonempty total intersection. Directedness supplies the finite-intersection property, and one family member provides a compact ambient subset for the argument. The separate closedness assumptions make this Cantor intersection statement valid without Hausdorffness. [Khatchatourian](https://www.math.toronto.edu/ivan/mat327/docs/notes/17-tychonoff.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L328).

An ultrafilter containing a compact subset s converges to some point of s. Lean expresses containing s by f≤principal(s), and convergence by f≤nhds(x). This is the subset form of Kruckman’s ultrafilter convergence theorem; compactness supplies existence, while no uniqueness or Hausdorff conclusion is asserted. [Kruckman](https://akruckman.faculty.wesleyan.edu/files/2019/07/ultrafilters.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L144).

An arbitrary indexed product of compact spaces is compact in the product topology. Factors may differ with the index, and the index set need not be finite. This is Tychonoff’s theorem, obtained by taking coordinate limits of ultrafilters. No Hausdorffness or nonemptiness of the factors is assumed; empty products are included. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1175).

The inverse image of a compact set under a closed embedding is compact. Intersect the set with the closed image of the embedding; this remains compact. The domain is homeomorphic to that image, so compactness transfers back. This is the closed-subspace theorem, with no Hausdorff assumptions needed. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1016).

A subset of the domain of a topological embedding is compact exactly when its image is compact. An embedding identifies its domain homeomorphically with its image carrying the subspace topology; restricting that homeomorphism transfers compactness in both directions. This is the usual invariance of compactness under homeomorphism, without separation assumptions. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L997).

The quotient of a compact space by any equivalence relation is compact in the quotient topology. The projection sending each point to its equivalence class is continuous and surjective. Its image is therefore compact and equals the entire quotient, giving exactly Wendl’s continuous-image corollary for arbitrary equivalence relations. [Wendl](https://www.math.hu-berlin.de/~wendl/Sommer2026/Topologie1/lecturenotes.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L1213).

A nontrivial filter containing a compact subset has a cluster point in that subset. A cluster point means every neighborhood meets every filter member; f≤principal(s) means s belongs to the filter. Nontrivial means the filter excludes the empty set. This matches White’s filter-base characterization of compactness. [White](https://personal.denison.edu/~whiteda/files/Lecture%20Notes/Ultrafilters.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L39).

A ring has an additive abelian group and associative multiplication with an identity, satisfying both distributive laws. Multiplication need not commute, and the zero ring is allowed. Natural numbers are interpreted by repeated addition of one, and negative integers by additive inverses; different integers may represent the same ring element. Compared with [the reference](https://maths.ucd.ie/~astier/mst20010/notes-mst20010.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L146).

Semiring has a commutative additive monoid, an associative multiplicative monoid, both distributive laws and an absorbing zero. The source includes the zero-absorption laws explicitly; they are not inferred from distributivity alone. Additive inverses, multiplicative commutativity and distinctness of zero and one are deliberately not required. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L141).

A commutative ring has an additive abelian group and associative, commutative multiplication with an identity, satisfying both distributive laws. The additional commutativity concerns multiplication. Zero divisors and the zero ring remain allowed; inverses for nonzero elements and cancellation of nonzero factors are separate requirements. Compared with [the reference](https://maths.ucd.ie/~astier/mst20010/notes-mst20010.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L413).

CommSemiring adds commutative multiplication to Semiring, matching the usual commutative-semiring convention. Addition remains a commutative monoid and zero remains absorbing. The class permits the trivial semiring and semirings without subtraction; multiplicative inverses, additive cancellation and idempotence of addition are all separate possible properties. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L228).

A nonassociative ring has an additive abelian group, a multiplicative identity and both distributive laws. Multiplication is not required to be associative, but associative rings are still included. Integers are interpreted using repeated addition of one and additive inverses, and multiplication by zero gives zero. Compared with [the reference](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25156/25156-pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L135).

NonUnitalRing is an additive abelian group with associative multiplication satisfying both distributive laws. It does not require a distinguished multiplicative identity, but does not forbid one. This matches the nonunital-ring convention; zero absorption is retained and does not require a unit or multiplicative commutativity. Compared with [the reference](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25156/25156-pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L132).

This is an additive abelian group with multiplication satisfying both distributive laws. Neither a multiplicative identity nor associativity is required, matching the general nonassociative-ring convention. Multiplication by zero gives zero, as follows from distributivity and additive cancellation. Ordinary associative rings with an identity are also included. Compared with [the reference](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25156/25156-pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L129).

This structure has commutative addition with an identity zero, multiplication satisfying both distributive laws, and zero absorbing multiplication on either side. Neither a multiplicative identity nor associativity is required. Additive inverses are also unnecessary; zero absorption is required explicitly because distributivity alone does not imply it. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L119).

This is an additive abelian group with commutative multiplication satisfying both distributive laws. Multiplication need not be associative or have an identity. Commutativity does not imply either missing property; ordinary commutative rings with an identity are nevertheless included because these properties are optional, rather than forbidden. Compared with [the reference](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25156/25156-pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L392).

Distrib records exactly left and right distributivity of multiplication over addition. The factors stay in their original order in both equations, so noncommutative multiplication is handled correctly. Neither operation is assumed associative or commutative, and no zero, unit, inverse or cancellation law is included. Compared with [the reference](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25156/25156-pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L62).

IsDomain requires a nontrivial semiring with cancellation by every nonzero factor on both sides. Its documentation states this stronger semiring formulation explicitly. For commutative rings, subtraction makes it equivalent to having no nonzero zero divisors, agreeing with the cited Stacks definition of an integral domain. Compared with [the reference](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09FE) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L437).

Right distributivity says (a+b)*c=a*c+b*c: multiplying a sum on the right multiplies each summand on the right. The declaration assumes precisely this distributive law for the supplied addition and multiplication. No ring, associativity or commutativity hypothesis is needed, and the order of factors is preserved. Compared with [the reference](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/25156/25156-pdf.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Defs.lean#L97).

A division semiring has zero distinct from one and multiplicative inverses for every nonzero element; multiplication need not commute. Inverse of zero is defined as zero. Nonnegative rationals are interpreted as numerator divided by denominator; a denominator becoming zero gives zero. The algebra over ℚ≥0 requires characteristic zero. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Field/Defs.lean#L86).

A semifield is a commutative semiring with zero distinct from one and inverses for nonzero elements. Additive inverses are unnecessary, although fields are included. Inverse of zero is defined as zero. Nonnegative rationals mean numerator divided by denominator, giving zero if that denominator becomes zero in the semifield. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Field/Defs.lean#L168).

MonoidWithZero is an associative multiplicative monoid with a distinguished two-sided absorbing element zero. This agrees with the standard monoid-with-zero notion. It does not require zero and one to differ or nonzero elements to be invertible; the singleton monoid is therefore a valid boundary case. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L125).

The designated element zero absorbs multiplication on both sides: 0*a=0 and a*0=0. These are exactly the two required equations. Addition is not supplied, so this zero need not be an additive identity. No multiplicative identity, associativity or commutativity assumption is needed. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L38).

Multiplication has a two-sided identity one and a two-sided absorbing element zero: 1*a=a=a*1 and 0*a=0=a*0. Associativity is not required. Zero and one may coincide, forcing a one-element structure. Addition, inverses, commutativity and cancellation are separate requirements and are not part of this definition. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L121).

A semigroup with zero has associative multiplication and an element zero satisfying 0*a=0=a*0. This matches the usual definition. A multiplicative identity is not required, and zero may already belong to the original structure. One-element examples and multiplication that is always zero are both permitted. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L118).

A nonzero factor can be cancelled from either side of an equality: a*b=a*c implies b=c when a≠0, and b*a=c*a gives the same conclusion. Multiplication and a designated zero are supplied. Associativity and absorption by zero are not required; the cancellation hypothesis deliberately excludes the zero factor. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L100).

IsLeftCancelMulZero requires left multiplication by each nonzero element to be injective. Thus a*b=a*c implies b=c when a≠0, with the cancelled factor correctly on the left. Right cancellation, associativity, zero absorption and invertibility are not asserted by this isolated property. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Defs.lean#L48).
